approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (Excise Charges Imposition) Bill 2025
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is one of three in a package that would create a legal framework for charging fees related to administering the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999.
The specific fees and their amounts would be set by regulations, and the minister must ensure each fee recovers no more than the government's expected costs for that activity.
The package splits the fees into three separate bills because the Australian Constitution requires excise, customs and other taxes to be in different Acts.
Creates a framework for imposing charges on activities under the EPBC Act.
Limits charges to cost recovery, with the minister required to verify amounts do not exceed the Commonwealth's likely costs.
Splits charges into three bills based on constitutional categories: excise, customs and general.
People and businesses that engage in activities regulated under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999.

Moved that the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (Excise Charges Imposition) Bill 2025 be read a second time, explaining that regulations will set cost-recovery charges for prescribed activities after consultation and urging action on a long-delayed response.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to expedite debate and voting on seven environment bills, including limiting consideration in detail to five minutes per amendment set unless extended by a minister, and moved that the question be put.

Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders and set the day's business, including immediate consideration of the Environment Protection Reform Bill and related bills, specified times for second reading and remaining stages, permitted divisions after 4.30 pm, and subsequent consideration of listed Senate business.
